document.title: Terrorist Attack on USS Cole: Background and Issues for Congress
document.authors: Raphael Perl and Ronald O'Rourke, Congressional Research Service
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Terrorism and U.S. Policy
document.note: [Unclassified] Brief background on the October 12, 2000 attack on the USS Cole. It examines issues for Congress, including force protection procedures, intelligence on potential attacks and overall U.S. anti-terrorism policy.

events.description: USS Cole attacked by a small boat laden with explosives in Aden harbor; 17 crew killed, 39 wounded.
Crouch-Gehman DoD panel issued report finding security shortcomings without assigning blame.
Commander of the Atlantic Fleet released Navy investigation results.
John Warner announced SASC would hold its own investigation.
Gen. Tommy Franks testified before SASC on the decision to refuel in Aden.
US retaliatory attack on Afghanistan after East Africa embassy bombings.
US Navy ships began refueling stops in Aden.
U.S. Central Command signed a refueling contract adding Aden, Yemen, bringing ports available in its AOR to 13, after Djibouti deteriorated due to the Eritrea-Ethiopia war.
Embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania.
Attack on USS Cole in Aden; no specific threat information had been received for Yemen or Aden beforehand.
General Franks gave opening remarks to the Senate Armed Services Committee on the refueling decision.
State Department worldwide terrorism report characterized Yemen as a haven for terrorists.
U.S. cruise missile attack on a pharmaceutical factory in Sudan in response to embassy bombings, viewed by some as a mistake.
U.S. retaliatory attack on Afghanistan following the East Africa embassy bombings.
U.S. Navy ships began refueling stops in Aden.
Central Command decided to use Yemen (Aden) for refueling rather than Djibouti; a refueling contract was signed.
Embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania, cited as part of Horn of Africa turmoil.
State Department report on worldwide terrorism characterized Yemen as a haven for terrorists.
Attack on USS Cole in Aden harbor.
Gen. Franks testified before the Senate Armed Services Committee on the Cole attack and the Aden refueling decision.
Suicide boat bomb attack on USS Cole during refueling stop, killing 17 crew and wounding 39.
Truck-bomb attack on U.S. Marine Corps barracks in Beirut, cited as precedent.
Truck-bomb attack on Khobar Towers U.S. military residence, cited as precedent.
Crouch-Gehman DoD panel issued report avoiding blame but finding shortcomings in security, training and intelligence.
Commander of the Atlantic Fleet released Navy investigation results concluding security plan procedures were not followed but attack could not have been prevented.
Senate Armed Services Committee Chairman Warner announced the committee's own investigation.
At least six suspects held in custody in Yemen.
USS Cole entered service.

key_claims: Evidence suggests the Cole attack may have been carried out by Islamic militants with possible connections to Usama bin Ladin's network.
The attack was a boat-bomb adaptation of earlier truck-bomb tactics at Beirut 1983 and Khobar Towers 1996.
At least six suspects were in custody in Yemen.
The FBI led the investigation jointly with Yemeni officials.
The Bin Ladin network is believed responsible for several anti-U.S. attacks since 1992.
The August 1998 US strike on Afghanistan did little to damage Bin Ladin's network or planning ability.
